evals.name: transformer-talk
evals.prompt: I'm giving a 15-minute talk at our ML reading group about the Transformer architecture from 'Attention Is All You Need'. Make me a slide deck of about 10 slides in Typst. I want an architecture diagram of the Transformer, the scaled dot-product attention formula, and a comparison table against RNNs/CNNs. Cite the key papers properly. Don't ask me any questions — make reasonable choices yourself and note your assumptions. Deliver the .typ source and the compiled PDF.
evals.expected_output: A ~10-slide 16:9 Metropolis deck: typst default fonts, a fletcher/cetz architecture diagram that fits the slide, attention formula in math, comparison table, footnote citations, references slide. PDF compiles clean.
assertions: Deck uses Touying with the Metropolis theme
Architecture diagram is drawn (fletcher/cetz or generated figure)

evals.name: surface-code-journal-club
evals.prompt: Prepare journal-club slides introducing the surface code for quantum error correction — about 8 slides, in Typst. Include: a short stabilizer formalism recap, a distance-3 surface code layout figure, the syndrome extraction circuit drawn as a quantum circuit diagram, and an interactive link the audience can click to explore that circuit in a browser. Cite foundational papers (e.g. Kitaev, Fowler et al.). Don't ask me questions; decide and note your assumptions. Deliver the .typ source and the compiled PDF.
evals.expected_output: A ~8-slide deck with a quill syndrome-extraction circuit, a surface-code lattice figure (cetz or stim SVG), a clickable Quirk URL for the syndrome-extraction gadget, footnote citations, references slide.
assertions: Deck uses Touying with the Metropolis theme
Syndrome-extraction circuit drawn as a quantum circuit

evals.name: benchmark-results-deck
evals.prompt: Turn the benchmark results in bench.csv into a 5-slide results deck for my advisor, in Typst: a title slide, one summary slide with the headline finding, a chart comparing throughput across the three implementations at 1 and 8 threads, a table with the raw numbers, and a conclusions slide. Deliver the .typ source and the compiled PDF.
evals.expected_output: A ~5-slide deck: chart of throughput (lilaq or external tool), table matching CSV values, headline identifying lockfree_mpmc as fastest at 8 threads.
assertions: Deck uses Touying with the Metropolis theme
A throughput chart is generated (lilaq/cetz-plot/external figure)
Raw CSV values appear in the table (96.5, 71.2, 18.9)
Headline names the lock-free implementation as fastest at 8 threads
